note: The globe is cobe (MIT, 12.9 KB, vendored at assets/vendor/cobe.module.js), and the reason it is safe to use is measured rather than assumed: its published build contains zero requestAnimationFrame, zero performance.now and zero Date.now. It owns no clock, so `phi = f(t)` is the entire integration and determinism is a property of the shape rather than a contract someone has to remember. Magic UI's globe is a React wrapper around this same library; we use the library, not the wrapper, so no React enters the engine and its rAF spring loop, which is exactly the thing we must not have, is simply not part of it. The three.js globe in core/three-fx.js stays for the one thing cobe cannot do, a terminator computed as a real hemisphere from a sun vector. This one is prettier and is a tenth of the code. PACING, after measuring: the first cut of this ran twenty seconds at 0.85 events per second, slower than the film it replaces (1.79) and below the library's median (1.20). The cause was not too few layers, it was too much time: a route that took 9.2s to draw and a camera settling over 11s, neither of which reads as motion. It is 13s now with the same content, and the first thing cut was duration.

audio._why: As showcase-flight-computed.json: the film wants a bed that lifts with the light, and shipping the wrong one is worse than shipping none. A gap, stated, not a claim that mute is better.

_bg_why: plain was a decision nobody made. This is the light-mode mesh wash, but the stock gradientWash pools are cobalt at alpha 0.78 and at that strength the backdrop turned half the frame blue and fought the route, which is the one cobalt thing that matters. So the blobs are hand-set: mostly the theme's line grey, one cobalt pool at alpha 0.09, and periods of 9 to 13 seconds so the field actually travels within a 13s film instead of creeping. Judged on the beat sheet across five beats, never on one still.
_cuts_why: NONE. The argument is one object that never leaves, and a cut is a moment it does not survive. Two fades over a globe that is mid-draw were furniture: they marked beats the copy already marks, and the direction floor was right to call the result a slideshow by construction, because the only thing crossing those junctions was a canvas whose change it cannot see. Removing them makes the claim true rather than waived. Beat boundaries are carried entirely by copy arriving and leaving over a route that keeps drawing.

layers._colors_why: light mode, from themes/vawe.json: sea #f6f8fb (bg2, so the planet sits ON the page) · marker+route #2563eb (accent, on white the accent is the strongest value the theme owns, and the route is the subject) · glow #e7eaf0 (line, a hairline halo rather than a bloom). dark:0 because a shaded night side on a white page reads as dirt.

layers.text: one JSON · 780 frames · identical every run

_why.aphoristic-cadence: The rule would have me cut "Every vertex computed. Not one drawn." as manufactured contrast, and it is right about the shape. Here the contrast is the fact: the globe is 22,000 points sampled from Natural Earth and a great-circle route solved per frame, and there is no drawn artwork anywhere in the film. The rule exists to make the author decide rather than comply. This is the decision.
_why.no-storyboard: legacy: grandfathered 2026-08-21, adopted 2026-08-21 (the film has a written plan (a storyboard, declared or found beside it))
_why.no-preflight: legacy: grandfathered 2026-08-28, adopted 2026-08-28 (the film went through the decision chain before the JSON existed)
_why.no-transition: legacy: grandfathered 2026-09-04, adopted 2026-09-04 (a multi-beat film earns at least one real seam or cut, not flat jumps)
